rites.name: Vornia
rites.text: A practiced fighting method in which a warrior hurls an opponent down onto the ground. It is taught as a skill of close combat.

rites.name: Ristanum
rites.text: Ristanum is the concept of a trial held in the Courts of Osutaala, where a verdict is weighed against the whole of an accused's measured will. In the Era of the Record it was the principle that a door between worlds opens only when the council has judged the ground beneath it sound. Its adherents describe it less as a power than as a standard that the powers of the Courts must answer to.

rites.name: Fenodureld
rites.text: Fenodureld is a concept within Osutaala, a idea of flame-bound judgment that the Courts of the Holy Age used to test the worthiness of those who sought passage between worlds. It is remembered as a pattern of burning trial rather than a single figure, shaping the temples and orders that kept the doors in order.

rites.name: Sereosum
rites.text: A wielder channels an inner life-force into a forceful strike aimed at a rival. Fighters rarely rely on it, but when they do, it is followed by a flurry of additional kicks.

rites.name: Rinanum
rites.text: Beings of a hidden kin draw in their shared essence through sharp teeth and pass it into another through the blood. The receiver is mended when weak, and a human so treated is slowly transformed into one of the kin.

rites.name: Taureornus
rites.text: A bloodborne craft lets its wielders reshape their bodies into nearly any form they choose, including beasts, swarms, and vapor drawn from old legends.

rites.name: Vaulles
rites.text: A hidden current that powers all the creatures of the wild folk, granting them strength, swiftness, endurance, and quick mending beyond ordinary flesh. Its strength differs widely between kinds, and creatures can feel it in one another, sensing who is nearby.

rites.name: Orases
rites.text: A bloodline gift lets its bearer blend inner life-force with their own lifeblood and shape the mixture by will. Users can form solid armor from it or unleash violent bursts that can shatter even the mightiest foes.

rites.name: Telerus
rites.text: A bound inner power that a wielder can unlock in a deeper stage, sharply raising speed and strength. Its use risks letting an ancestral blood force take over the wielder's mind.

rites.name: Anaranuta
rites.text: Anaranuta is a dormant gravitational art in the Ki realm of Osutaala, a discipline that folds local spacetime into a single razor edge capable of severing orbits. Practitioners treat it as a last resort, since a poorly drawn stroke can tear open the ground beneath them as readily as it does the enemy.

rites.name: Vanalanum
rites.text: Vanalanum is a concept of pure stillness in the Ki realm of Osutaala, a discipline that severs the seams a technique uses to slip between layers of reality. Its practitioners teach that a cut which leaves no shadow cannot be crossed, so any attack relying on a folded path simply stalls at the blade's edge. It is taught as a defense more than a weapon, though its students swear it can end a strike before it arrives.

rites.name: Ukavasaluta
rites.text: Ukavasaluta is a sweet-smelling mist-bloom that drifts over the highland meadows of the Ki realm, lulling anyone who breathes it into devoted obedience. Those who resist the bloom must be snared again and again, and a single kiss from the bloom's keeper seals the victim into servitude that outlasts any lifetime.

rites.name: Ukavameno
rites.text: Ukavameno is a sensing art that lets its wielder perceive every flow of spiritual charge within a wide sphere, pinpointing hidden souls and tracing them through any concealment. When the restraint upon the art is loosened, the perceiver can read the exact nature and magnitude of any power and reproduce it as her own.

rites.name: Tiralaroma
rites.text: Tiralaroma is a bound-life ritual fused into a single living ward-engine, kept alive by the cooling of a sealed kiln-heart. When its keeper's core is breached, the stored heat detonates outward, flattening a district but never reaching the walls of the surrounding city.

rites.name: Tenvamala
rites.text: Tenvamala is a ritual sealing-thread craft devised by the warden-scribe Ilsoren Vaad, who threads a practitioner's own will through one hundred and nine silver needles driven into a bound subject. The final needle, placed over the heart, halts breathing for a time while the reshaped channels settle, and failure is almost always fatal.

rites.name: Osutamnaira
rites.text: Osutamnaira is a binding ward of the Ki realm, a self-tightening lattice of sealed talismans that wraps a wielder in mechanical wings and reaching arms. Each swing or thrust multiplies its force, but the lattice clenches tighter with every movement and grinds the wearer's own frame. Its final form, a bundle of feather-shaped spears, can strike through the hide of a true-form god.

rites.name: Anasarkamum
rites.text: Anasarkamum is a concept of pure kinetic release, the principle that a body turning faster than it can hold itself together will hurl its stored motion outward as a shockwave. In the Ki realm of Osutaala it is taught as a discipline of spiraling the limbs, so that a single sharpened strike carries the weight of a falling ridge.

rites.name: Osunasanuta
rites.text: Osunasanuta is a sun-forged war-hammer hung on the belt of the wandering smith-saint Erevik Dorrand, who claims it was pounded out of a dying star's core. Those who lift it report feeling their own heartbeat slow to match the hammer's distant tolling.

rites.name: Ilosavamala
rites.text: Ilosavamala is a concept of the Ki realm in the E6 era, third age of its world Osutaala, where arcane will is bound into living metal. Its bearers are said to unfold feather-blades through a sealed shell of coiled iron to strike at foes already caught fast.

rites.name: Kalulaari
rites.text: Kalulaari is a concept of rhythmic force in the Ki realm of Osutaala, a discipline in which a single practitioner's pulse of strikes stacks into a cascade faster than heat can spread. Its strength is gated by sealed resonances that open one by one, and each one loosens the wielder's tempo so that more foes can be struck before the first has fallen.

rites.name: Suratalum
rites.text: Suratalum is a bound-spirit ritual in which a caster drives a sealed servitor-entity into the world by burning a private reservoir of inner ember as its toll. The entity arrives wrapped in a puff of gray vapor, and the vapor's thickness mirrors how deeply the caster is willing to spend. Pushed past empty, the rite feeds on the caster's own vital thread and slowly unmakes them.

rites.name: Ilokanala
rites.text: Ilokanala is a grimoire of recorded recipes that its keeper can bring into being through paper charms acting as conduits. Its variety is effectively boundless, though it offers little to a duel between two individuals.

rites.name: Suravareno
rites.text: Suravareno is a concept of stored ki in Osutaala's fourth age, a discipline that channels a single breath into the bedrock beneath a practitioner's feet. Its masters are said to release the whole charge through one stamp, lifting the ground in a rolling wave that catches airborne foes and hurls them backward. The art is honored as a close-range defense against flying attackers.

rites.name: Surasaala
rites.text: Surasaala is a shapeshifting spirit of the Ki realm who can wear any form it has witnessed, from a modest sparrow to a storm-wing colossus. Its most dangerous form is a sleek obsidian beast whose kin once tore open the sky above the Veyrun basin.

rites.name: Ukatanraeno
rites.text: Ukatanraeno is a dueling forms-technique of the Ki realm, sung as a paired sequence in which two practitioners answer each other's strikes until the final movement collapses both their energies into a single arc. It was refined in the third age of the E6 era, when wandering duelists sought a finisher that no single body could sustain.

rites.name: Osukanira
rites.text: Osukanira is a sealing discipline in the Osutaala realm of Ki, where practitioners bind raw spiritual current into lattices of glyphs that hold entire districts in suspension. Its most celebrated work is a sealed bell-tower that quietly contained a dying tide of wild ether for centuries.
